name: sweden-counties-and-provinces

description.en: Sweden's 21 counties and 25 provinces in 46 cards, in English and Swedish. A county card shows the county's name and asks for its seat (residensstad); a province card shows the province's name and asks for the land (landsdel) it traditionally belongs to: Götaland, Svealand or Norrland. Compiled from Wikidata and checked against the county administrative boards' websites, Nationalencyklopedin and Wikipedia.
description.sv: Sveriges 21 län och 25 landskap på 46 kort, på engelska och svenska. Ett länskort visar länets namn och frågar efter residensstaden; ett landskapskort visar landskapets namn och frågar efter landsdelen det traditionellt hör till: Götaland, Svealand eller Norrland. Sammanställd från Wikidata och kontrollerad mot länsstyrelsernas webbplatser, Nationalencyklopedin och Wikipedia.

method: The deck was researched, drafted and cross-checked by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks and independent AI review rounds, recorded under Quality control. No human subject expert has reviewed the cards yet.

Counties: the Wikidata Query Service (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) was asked for every instance of county of Sweden (Q200547) without a dissolution date (P576), with its English and Swedish labels, its seat (P36 capital) and the seat's English and Swedish labels, and its county code (P507) (query 1). It returned exactly 21 counties, one seat each. The card front is the county's English label ("Västra Götaland County") and Swedish label ("Västra Götalands län"), the back the seat's English and Swedish labels (English "Gothenburg", Swedish "Göteborg"; all other seats have the same name in both languages).

County seats were checked against the counties' own administrative boards: a script (command 4, given verbatim in Queries) fetched each board's start page https://www.lansstyrelsen.se/<county>.html, stripped scripts, styles and tags, and took the last match of the regular expressions Postadress (.{0,60}?) Telefon (postal address) and Besöksadress (.{0,60}?) Postadress (visiting address); in all 21 the town of the postal address is the Wikidata seat. The visiting-address pattern found nothing for Skåne, whose footer was then read by hand in the saved page. Skåne's board gives visiting addresses in both Kristianstad and Malmö, so its county residence page was read as well: governors have lived at Stortorget in Malmö since 1658 (with short exceptions); the card says Malmö and notes the Kristianstad office. Norrbotten's board also lists an office in Jokkmokk, with Luleå first. The government ordinance on the boards, Förordning (2017:868) med länsstyrelseinstruktion (https://data.riksdagen.se/dokument/sfs-2017-868.text, command 11), was also fetched and searched for the boards' seats; it does not name them, so it is not cited.
As an independent check, the raw wikitext of Swedish Wikipedia's article Sveriges län (command 5) was read: its table's Residensstad column agrees with Wikidata for all 21 counties.

Provinces: Wikidata was asked for every instance of province of Sweden (Q193556) with its English and Swedish labels and its P361/P131/P706 values (query 2), and for the provinces each land lists under P527 has part(s) (query 3: Götaland Q201694, Svealand Q203835, Norrland Q203505; the stray items were inspected with command 10). Query 2 returned the 25 provinces plus two stray items: Q19400650 (no labels, different from Gotland Q1027830) and Q10376643 (a second Södermanland item, labelled Södermanland in English and Swedish and described only as "landskap", duplicating Q626062), both left out. The provinces' own P361 statements name a land for only three of them, so the land was taken from the lands' P527 lists, which cover all 25 except as described in step 7.

Each province's land was checked against two independent tables: Swedish Wikipedia's Landskap i Sverige (column Landsdel, command 6) and English Wikipedia's Provinces of Sweden (per-land lists in the Heraldry section, command 7). Both agree on 10 provinces in Götaland, 6 in Svealand and 9 in Norrland, Lappland in Norrland. Swedish Wikipedia's Svealand article (command 8) was read for Värmland's history. As a non-Wikimedia check, the freely visible lead sentences of Nationalencyklopedin's articles Götaland, Svealand and Norrland (command 14) list the same 10, 6 and 9 provinces. The deck uses this traditional division by province; the natural-geography border of Norrland (limes norrlandicus) and the county-based statistical regions differ from it.

Wikidata's P527 statements and their qualifiers (query 3 uses truthy wdt:P527, which does not show qualifiers, so the claims were also read with wbgetclaims, query 12): Värmland is listed under Götaland with end time (P582) 1815 and under Svealand with start time (P580) 1815, so Wikidata agrees with the other sources that Värmland is in Svealand today. Swedish Wikipedia also says Värmland was counted to Götaland until 1815; English Wikipedia says until 1812. The card gives Svealand, with the note "formerly counted as part of Götaland" (no year, since the sources disagree), and checks Svealand's P527. Svealand's P527 also lists Åland (Q5689) with end time 1809-09-17 (Treaty of Fredrikshamn, when Åland was ceded to Russia); it is not a Swedish province today and plays no part, since the province list comes from the instances of Q193556, not from the lands' P527. Götaland's P527 lists the island Öland (Q239276) instead of the province item Q15981396, so the Öland card has label checks only; both Wikipedia tables and Nationalencyklopedin put the province in Götaland.

Card text: fronts are "<English name> (province)" and "<Swedish name> (landskap)" for provinces, so a province is never confused with the county of the same name (Gotland, Jämtland, Norrbotten and others). English names are Wikidata's English labels (Scania for Skåne and Lapland for Lappland; the rest keep the Swedish name in English). The back label says what is asked: Seat / Residensstad, Land / Landsdel. The lands are called Götaland, Svealand and Norrland in both languages.

Every card carries Wikidata checks (command 9 runs them): the English and Swedish labels on the card, the county's P36 seat, the land's labels and, except Öland, the land's P527 statement that lists the province. The notes added after review are checked where Wikidata states them: the former Älvsborg County's labels, seat (P36) and dissolution year (P576).

Notes added after review round 1 and 2: the Västra Götaland note (Vänersborg, the former Älvsborg County's seat until 1997) rests on Wikidata Q254990 (P36 Vänersborg, P576 1998-01-01) and is checked against Swedish Wikipedia's Residensstad; the Västernorrland and Södermanland notes (the seat is not the largest town) rest on Wikidata's municipal populations (P1082, query 13) and Swedish Wikipedia's Residensstad, and the board's contact pages were read for Västra Götaland's offices. The Scania and Lapland notes give the Swedish or English name from the Wikidata labels already on the cards.
selection: All of Sweden's 21 present counties (län) and all 25 provinces (landskap): a complete, closed set, so nothing was selected or left out by judgement. Two card kinds only: county → seat (residensstad) and province → land (landsdel). Not included: dissolved counties (e.g. Malmöhus and Kristianstads län), the counties' letters and codes, and the province → county relation, since many provinces lie in several counties and such a card would have no single answer. Two stray Wikidata items typed as provinces (Q19400650, Q10376643) were excluded as duplicates or empty items.

queries.query:
"""Fetch each county administrative board's start page on lansstyrelsen.se and print the
postal address (Postadress) in its footer, which names the town of the board's head office."""
import re
import time
import urllib.request

SLUGS = ["stockholm", "uppsala", "sodermanland", "ostergotland", "jonkoping", "kronoberg", "kalmar",
         "gotland", "blekinge", "skane", "halland", "vastra-gotaland", "varmland", "orebro",
         "vastmanland", "dalarna", "gavleborg", "vasternorrland", "jamtland", "vasterbotten", "norrbotten"]
OUT = "./"
for slug in SLUGS:
    url = f"https://www.lansstyrelsen.se/{slug}.html"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"})
    html = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60).read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    open(f"{OUT}lst-{slug}.html", "w").write(html)
    t = re.sub(r"<script.*?</script>|<style.*?</style>", "", html, flags=re.S)
    t = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", t)
    t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t).replace(" ", " ")
    m = re.findall(r"Postadress (.{0,60}?) Telefon", t)
    b = re.findall(r"Besöksadress (.{0,60}?) Postadress", t)
    print(slug, "| Postadress:", m[-1] if m else None, "| Besöksadress:", b[-1] if b else None)
    time.sleep(1)

licensing: Everything in the cards comes from Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the list of counties and provinces, their English and Swedish names, the seats and the lands. The set is the complete set of Sweden's counties and provinces, so no selection was taken from anywhere. The county boards' websites and Nationalencyklopedin (all rights reserved) and the Wikipedia articles (CC BY-SA 4.0) were only consulted to confirm the facts; no text, wording or selection was copied from them, and the card wording ("X (province)", the back labels and notes) is the compilers' own. Facts are not copyrightable, so the deck can be released under CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library.
